channel.title: The Byte Log
channel.description: Practical notes on software, home labs and the tools in between.

item.title: SQLite in WAL mode: what actually changes
item.author: editor@example.com (The Byte Log)
item.description:
Write-ahead logging lets readers keep reading while a writer commits, which is exactly what a small self-hosted app wants. We walk through checkpoints, the -wal file, and why a single connection is often the simplest safe choice.

Plus: how to take a consistent backup without stopping the server.

item.title: The 3-2-1 backup rule for a house full of devices
item.description:
Three copies, two kinds of media, one off-site. It sounds like enterprise advice, but it maps neatly onto a NAS, an external drive in a drawer, and a cheap object-storage bucket.

  • Automate the first two.
  • Test a restore every quarter.
  • Write down where the keys are.

item.title: Keeping a Raspberry Pi 5 cool and quiet
item.description: The official active cooler is good, but a passive aluminium case is silent and keeps sustained workloads under the throttling point in most rooms. We measured both over a week of running a home server.

item.title: Why your Wi-Fi slows down at 7pm
item.description: Everyone on your street starts streaming at once. Channel congestion, band steering and a router in the wrong cupboard all play a part. A ten-minute survey with a free analyser app usually finds the fix.

item.title: Passkeys for the whole family, one year on
item.description: What worked, what confused the kids, and the one account recovery scare that made us print a set of backup codes and put them in the safe.

item.title: Server-rendered HTML is having a moment
item.description: Small libraries that swap fragments of HTML over the wire have made plain server-side templates feel modern again. A look at the patterns that keep such apps fast: out-of-band swaps, history support, and progressive enhancement.

item.title: Self-hosting an RSS reader in 2026
item.description: Feeds never went away. With a single binary and a SQLite file you can follow a hundred sites without an algorithm deciding what you see first.

item.title: Context cancellation in Go, explained with a kettle
item.description: You put the kettle on, then the phone rings. A friendly walk through context.WithCancel, deadlines, and why every blocking call in a server should take a context.
